title: Mihin and minne: answering with -lle
focus: Use mihin or minne for a destination in the at/on family too. Mihin sinä menet? — Menen asemalle.
prerequisiteSkills: Mihin and minne: answering with common into-forms

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Where are you going?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The illative is an into/to form; mihin aikaan uses that form in a time expression. Use mihin or minne for a destination in the at/on family too. The ending -lle means to or onto: asemalle (“to the station”), pöydälle (“onto the table”). It has no vowel-harmony variant. The complete question means “Where are you going”.

sentenceExplanation.translation: Where are you going?
sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking where to + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.formation: Mihin is the illative question form; in mihin aikaan it instead asks at what time.
